answer: The knoll multiplier is published, charged in lantern, and glacier lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 19 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 3203 identities would post 2308 proofs and burn roughly 36 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
